block_instructions: Never run `git reset`: Every form moves HEAD and can orphan commits, eventually lost to GC.
Never run `git clean (-[A-Za-z]*f|--force)`: Deletes untracked files irrecoverably; only the force forms delete.

Never run `git branch( +[^ ]+)* +(-[A-Za-z]*[dDmMfC]|--(delete|move|force))`: Deletes, renames, force-moves or force-copies a branch, which throws away a ref the user made. Creating one is a git write too, which agents leave to the user.
Never run `git tag( +[^ ]+)* +(-[A-Za-z]*[df]|--(delete|force))`: Deletes or force-moves a tag, which throws away a ref the user made. Others can already have fetched that tag.

Never run `git checkout`: Changes the branch or checkout this session works in. Every agent and subagent stays on the branch and checkout the session started in, plans included; only the user changes branches or worktrees. Give the user the exact command instead. Its `--` form also overwrites files with no reflog to recover them.
Never run `git (checkout-index|read-tree|sparse-checkout)`: Writes files into the checkout or the index, or changes which files the checkout has. No reflog keeps the old state.
Never run `git restore`: Always rewrites index or worktree; no variant is safe enough to allow.
Never run `git stash`: Moves uncommitted work somewhere the user did not put it.

Never run `git switch`: Changes the branch or checkout this session works in. Every agent and subagent stays on the branch and checkout the session started in, plans included; only the user changes branches or worktrees. Give the user the exact command instead.

Never run `git bisect`: Changes the branch or checkout this session works in. Every agent and subagent stays on the branch and checkout the session started in, plans included; only the user changes branches or worktrees. Give the user the exact command instead.
Never run `git rebase`: Rewrites history that may already be shared.
Never run `git filter-(branch|repo)`: Rewrites every commit in the history. Others can already have pulled those commits.
Never run `git pull( +[^ ]+)* +(-[A-Za-z]*r|--rebase)`: Rebases local commits onto the fetched branch, which rewrites them.
Never run `git( +[^ ]+)* +--abort$`: Stops a merge, cherry-pick, revert, am or rebase and puts the tree back to its state before the operation. Changes made since then can be lost.
Never run `git commit( +[^ ]+)* +--amend`: Rewrites the last commit, in any flag order; a plain commit stays allowed.
Never run `git rm`: Removes tracked files from the worktree, not just the index.
Never run `git gc`: Prunes unreachable objects that are the recovery path for a bad reset.
Never run `git prune`: Same recovery-path destruction as gc.
Never run `git reflog (expire|delete|drop)`: The reflog is the last thing standing after a destructive command.
Never run `git update-ref`: Moves refs beneath the porcelain, bypassing every other guard.

Never run `git symbolic-ref( +[^ ]+)* +(-[A-Za-z]*d|--delete|[^ ]*HEAD +refs/)`: Points HEAD at another branch with no checkout, or deletes a symbolic ref. A read with one name, such as `git symbolic-ref --short HEAD` or `git symbolic-ref --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`, stays allowed.

Never run `git worktree (add|move)`: Changes the branch or checkout this session works in. Every agent and subagent stays on the branch and checkout the session started in, plans included; only the user changes branches or worktrees. Give the user the exact command instead.

Never run `git worktree (remove|prune)`: Deletes a checkout that may hold uncommitted work, or the admin data that finds one. Only `list` is a read; `add` and `move` are git writes, which agents leave to the user.

Never run `git push( +[^ ]+)* +(-[A-Za-z]*[fd]|--(force|delete|mirror|prune)|\+|:)`: Force-pushes, or deletes or prunes refs on the remote, which others may already have pulled. A plain push, `-u`, `--follow-tags` and a `HEAD:refs/heads/<branch>` refspec stay allowed.
Never run `git fetch( +[^ ]+)* +(-[A-Za-z]*f|--force|\+)`: Force-updates local branches or tags, which can throw away commits. A `+` refspec, as in `origin +main:main`, also forces the update.

Never run `wt (switch|remove|merge|step|hook)`: Changes the branch or checkout this session works in. Every agent and subagent stays on the branch and checkout the session started in, plans included; only the user changes branches or worktrees. Give the user the exact command instead. `wt list` is a read.

Never run `gh pr (checkout|co|merge)` or `gh repo sync`: Changes the branch or checkout this session works in. Every agent and subagent stays on the branch and checkout the session started in, plans included; only the user changes branches or worktrees. Give the user the exact command instead.
Never run `gh pr close( +[^ ]+)* +(-d|--delete-branch)`: Deletes the local and remote branch of the pull request, which only the user does. Give the user the command.
Never run `gh repo (delete|archive|rename)`: Deletes, archives or renames a repository on GitHub, which changes it for every user. Give the user the command.
Never run `gh release (delete|delete-asset)`: Deletes a release or its files on GitHub. Others can already use them.
Never run `gh api( +[^ ]+)* +(-X *|--method[ =])DELETE`: Sends a DELETE request, which deletes data on GitHub, such as a branch, a tag or a release.
Each rule above also holds after a global option, as in `git -C <dir> reset`, `git -c <key>=<value> push --force` or `wt -C <path> switch`.
Agents read git, and add, commit and push once asked. Never run another git write; give the user the commands instead.
